races.name: Celebrating National Racehorse Week Maiden Hurdle Race (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: St Just In Time
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with solid form at 2m (2nd at 2m at Goodwood), Harry Derham's 6yo handles Good ground well (sim-going record 5/13 with 0W2P) and arrives fresh on 12 days' rest; Paul O'Brien picks up the ride and the patient style suits a slowly-run race where late energy is at a premium.

runners_data.name: Wait At The Gate
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 7yo with a win and a second from just four starts, Bradley Bridgwater's charge is 42 days fresh and carries the experience concern of a short form record; the single comparable run on Good ground produced a fourth, but the ⚠ lightly raced flag means potential upside if that fitness is intact.

runners_data.name: Iwanttobreakfree
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's 4yo is the race's lone confirmed front-runner and Harry Skelton will be able to dictate completely unchallenged; two placed efforts on Good at 2m (both 16f) show comfort with the conditions, though this will be the first time the horse faces the pressure of truly leading from flag to finish without a companion.

runners_data.name: Nightflyer
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr. rides this prominent-style 4yo who won on Soft over 2m and has placed twice on Good ground at the same trip; a 77-day absence and a sequence of poor runs (form: 1540-5) including a pulled-up effort raise fitness and consistency doubts, and Newton Abbot's tight track may catch a horse who travels well but struggles to sustain an effort.

runners_data.name: Maria Mes
runners_data.note: Jamie Snowden's 5yo has finished fourth in all four recent runs on Good or Soft, suggesting a level, honest performer without a change of gear; the prominent style should see Gavin Sheehan tracking Iwanttobreakfree comfortably, but the lack of a winning breakthrough at this stage is a concern in what is still a weak maiden.

runners_data.name: Morissette
runners_data.note: Bryan Carver's 6yo has been off 116 days and carries a ⚠ fades in finish flag, which is a significant drawback in a race where the hold-up horses will be arriving with momentum late; D Summersby's quiet yard (T14: 0/2) offers little encouragement, and the single comparable recent run (8th on Soft over 18f) gives limited grounds for optimism.

races.paceDynamic: Iwanttobreakfree is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner maiden hurdle and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, Harry Skelton's mount will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on Good ground over 2m2½f at Newton Abbot. Nightflyer and Maria Mes will press from prominent positions, but neither is a natural front-runner and both are likely to settle just off the pace rather than challenge for it. At a measured tempo set by one uncontested leader, the race will be run at a rhythm that suits horses travelling well within themselves into the straight, where finishing quality over the final two flights becomes the decisive factor. This shape most strongly favours hold-up horses with a clean finishing kick — particularly St Just In Time — who can benefit from a steady early pace before being produced with energy in reserve.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Iwanttobreakfree Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Iwanttobreakfree dictates an uncontested, honest but sustainable gallop and the field fails to close the gap entering the straight.
scenarios.body: Skelton's mount bowls along in front at a metronomic pace, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, conserves enough energy to repel challengers at the business end; the Good ground suits a rhythm-based performance from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp Tiring Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace, though modest, proves just quick enough to leave the front-runner vulnerable over the final two flights.
scenarios.body: St Just In Time, held up by Paul O'Brien and arriving with a strong late run, and Wait At The Gate — lightly raced and sparingly campaigned — both emerge to overhaul a fading Iwanttobreakfree; hold-up types benefit most when leaders are caught late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Nightflyer or Maria Mes move into contention turning in and the leader is headed before the last.
scenarios.body: Jonjo O'Neill Jr. produces Nightflyer from close order to challenge, having travelled prominently throughout; this shape suits horses who have shown tactical speed and can quicken from off the shoulder of the leader.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Errors Reshuffle Outcome
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or a race incident significantly disrupts the expected order and an unconsidered runner benefits.
scenarios.body: Morissette, 116 days off and flagged for fading in finishes, or Maria Mes could benefit opportunistically from a muddled race; this scenario is low probability but hinges on the front-runner being checked or making a costly mistake at a hurdle.

watchPoints.text: Watch Iwanttobreakfree's jumping under pressure — if Harry Skelton's mount gets into a rhythm and stands up cleanly, an uncontested leader on Good ground at Newton Abbot can be very hard to peg back.

Monitor Nightflyer's starting price and market move — Jonjo O'Neill Jr. in the plate after a 77-day layoff can attract money, but the horse's recent form (pulled up, multiple failures) suggests confidence in the stable is low.

St Just In Time's positioning in the early stages is critical — if Paul O'Brien is caught wide or loses ground at the start, a hold-up horse in a slowly-run race over this course will have little room to make up the deficit.

Morissette's tendency to fade in the finish combined with 116 days off makes this runner one to watch as a potential non-finisher or tail-ender if the race develops any tempo at all in the back straight.

Wait At The Gate's lightly raced profile means any market support late should be noted — a horse with so few runs can be hard to read on form alone, and the 42-day break is not concerning if Bridgwater has targeted this spot.

races.name: Wotton Printers Newton Abbot Novices' Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Premier Fantasy
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with two wins from four Good-ground runs and a course win over 26f; runs off a career-high 100 OR after a 39-day break, and from the rear will need the pace to collapse to get into this at his natural distance.|

runners_data.name: Better Off Alone
runners_data.note: Martin Keighley's runner holds a strong STYLE_FIT of 0.93 as a prominent racer who can set the pace, but returns after a 165-day layoff and has zero wins from eight runs on similar Going — jumping fluently will be critical to sustaining his front-running role.|

runners_data.name: Knightsbridge
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr. takes the mount on a lightly-raced six-year-old boasting two wins from 11 Good-ground outings and a recent course victory over 3m — the 42-day turnaround looks ideal and his positive jumping style suits tracking a lone leader.|

runners_data.name: Lynsey Larue
runners_data.note: A 146lbs lightweight on the card, Lynsey Larue was a course winner over 3m on Good-to-Soft last time out, but her trainer Mrs C Williams has drawn a blank in four runners over the past fortnight and the 75-day break is a mild concern.|

runners_data.name: Flashy Boy
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose true running style sits further back than this map suggests — placed to midfield because there are more rearward types than the map accommodates; ran just seven days ago, has one place from five Good-ground runs, and the short turnaround combined with racing away from his comfort zone tempers expectations.|

races.paceDynamic: Better Off Alone is the lone confirmed front-runner in this five-runner novice handicap chase over 3m2f at Newton Abbot, and with no meaningful pressure likely to materialise early, this race shapes up as a controlled, steady gallop from the front. Knightsbridge and Premier Fantasy are prominent and hold-up types respectively, but neither is wired to go toe-to-toe with Better Off Alone from the outset, meaning the pace-setter can effectively dictate terms at a tempo of their choosing on Good ground. That uncontested lead is a significant tactical weapon over this extreme distance, as a horse allowed to bowl along at a sustainable rhythm can drain the finish out of hold-up rivals before they can mount a meaningful challenge. The shape firmly favours a horse who can travel prominently and stay in contact through the final circuit — Knightsbridge, who possesses proven Good-ground form at similar trips and strong recent winning form, is ideally placed tactically, while the true closers (Premier Fantasy, Lynsey Larue, Flashy Boy) will need something to go wrong up front to capitalise. Note that Flashy Boy, a genuine hold-up type, has been mapped to midfield because the field contains more rearward horses than the pace map can place at the back — in practice Flashy Boy is unlikely to be as prominent as shown.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Better Off Alone is allowed to control the pace unchallenged and sets a measured, jumping rhythm throughout the 3m2f trip.
scenarios.body: Better Off Alone pings fences and controls energy expenditure perfectly, but over this trip the winner is most likely a horse travelling prominently enough to pounce in the straight — Knightsbridge, with two wins from 11 Good-ground runs and a recent course win at a similar trip, is ideally suited to track and collar.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If Better Off Alone weakens significantly at the final fence leaving ground for closers to finish strongly.
scenarios.body: Premier Fantasy, a course winner at 3m2f on Good ground and in fine recent form with two wins from four, would have the profile to close strongly from the rear if the front-runner capitulates.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Better Off Alone sets an overly ambitious gallop and stops sharply, opening the race up for all hold-up types.
scenarios.body: Lynsey Larue, a course winner on Good-to-Soft and carrying only 146lbs, has the stamina profile to pick up the pieces, though her trainer has had no wins from four runners in the past 14 days.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Flashy Boy Challenges Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If Flashy Boy, naturally a hold-up type but mapped forward, manages to secure a prominent position and stalk the leader.
scenarios.body: This scenario is discounted because Flashy Boy is a genuine rearward horse racing out of role — his STYLE_FIT tag and redistribution signal he is unlikely to reproduce his best from a forward berth, having run 165 days ago and showing mixed form on Good ground.

watchPoints.text: Monitor Better Off Alone at every fence — if he jumps cleanly and is untroubled, Knightsbridge must be tracked throughout as the most likely beneficiary of a controlled gallop.
Premier Fantasy's hold-up style means he needs a collapse or a mistake from the leader to land a blow; watch his position entering the back straight on the final circuit.
Lynsey Larue is 12lbs better-off at the weights relative to Knightsbridge on adjusted terms — if she travels easily in mid-pack early, she could outrun her odds at a big price.
Flashy Boy ran only seven days ago and is racing out of his natural style; watch for early signs of sluggishness or reluctance to settle — either would effectively end his involvement.
The Good ground at Newton Abbot is confirmed across all seven races today — no surface deterioration is expected, so stamina rather than ground adaptability will separate these runners over 3m2f.

races.name: Itus Event Support Services Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Run Away Joe
runners_data.note: Returned a worrying form string including a pulled-up and a fall but did finish fourth on Good ground over 2m at Goodwood; a confirmed hold-up horse who fades in the finish according to pace flags, and 224 days off is a significant fitness query for Fergal O'Brien's raider at this trip.

runners_data.name: Buxted Reel
runners_data.note: The only genuine front-runner in this field and coming here in good order having run just 19 days ago; Stan Sheppard can exploit total positional freedom on a horse with six place efforts and a win on similar Good to Soft ground, and Newton Abbot's tight layout suits a horse who controls its own tempo.

runners_data.name: Most Wanted
runners_data.note: Has genuine class in this company — one win and two places from five outings on Good ground — but his natural finishing-kick style will be diluted by the small field forcing him closer to the pace than he'd like; the pace redistribution means his 0.92 style-fit score is a real discount to his raw figures.

runners_data.name: Linden Lane
runners_data.note: A consistent place-getter without a win but placed four times in five career starts; races from the rear as a matter of course and with a 7lb conditional in Miss Eleanor Williams, the navigational challenge in a compressed small field limits how much of a late run she can manufacture.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Days
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with headgear (tongue-strap) and modest form including a pull-up, and no wins or places on Good ground across recent history; the youngest horse in the race, he remains unexposed but his consistency does not yet inspire confidence and his Good-ground record reads 0W0P.

runners_data.name: Ask Peter
runners_data.note: Has been placed twice from seven career hurdle runs and shaped with promise when second over 2m1f on Good ground; a tongue-strap wearer who his trainer Anthony Honeyball ran 39 days ago, he is a hold-up type whose natural game is most effective when there is a strong gallop to chase — which this race may not provide.

runners_data.name: Estate Planning
runners_data.note: Has run five times on Good or Good-to-Soft and managed two minor places; a genuine hold-up runner wearing a tongue-strap whose last four starts include an 11th and an 8th on soft ground, and his best form sits on a surface easier than today's — the Good ground here is a mild concern given his sim-going score of just 5/15.

races.paceDynamic: Buxted Reel is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner novice limited handicap and, with no horse likely to seriously press him for the lead, he should control proceedings at a measured, sustainable gallop from the outset. The rest of the field is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types — Most Wanted, Linden Lane, Ask Peter, Estate Planning, Run Away Joe and Pivotal Days all prefer to race from the rear — meaning the early sections are unlikely to be pressured and Buxted Reel can dictate every gear change. Stan Sheppard can ensure the race is run on Buxted Reel's terms, setting a comfortable tempo through the early stages and deciding when to stretch the field from the front. The field holds substantially more hold-up types than can realistically be accommodated at the rear of such a small field — Most Wanted, Linden Lane, Ask Peter and Estate Planning are all genuine closers who will be mapped further forward than their natural inclination demands, compromising their ability to produce a telling late run. The tactical verdict is unambiguous: a single uncontested front-runner dictating a tractable gallop in a field of seven on Good ground on a tight track heavily favours the prominent-to-lead profile, and Buxted Reel holds every positional advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Buxted Reel Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Buxted Reel is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a pace that keeps the closers permanently out of their comfort zone.
scenarios.body: Sheppard dictates from the front on a horse who has shown he can front-run with credit at this trip and going, and the absence of any rival willing to challenge for the lead means the race is run entirely to his script; on a sharp track like Newton Abbot a front-runner who controls tempo is notoriously hard to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Launch Late Challenge
scenarios.trigger: If Buxted Reel sets a pace that proves generous enough to leave him vulnerable in the closing stages and the hold-up horses find daylight.
scenarios.body: Most Wanted and Ask Peter, both capable of finishing powerfully on Good ground, would be the primary beneficiaries if the front-runner's advantage erodes turning for home; however, their chances are tempered by the likelihood they will be forced to race closer than ideal in a small field, reducing the run they can produce.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to string the field out and a horse tracking in mid-division picks the right moment to commit.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting three to four lengths off the lead in a small field has a natural position advantage over the true hold-up runners who must come from further back; Pivotal Days, racing in a more prominent role than its style label suggests, could capitalise if fitness holds on the back of a recent run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Tied Up Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop Buxted Reel sets proves too ambitious and he capitulates at the final hurdle or on the run-in.
scenarios.body: In a small field with a single pace-setter, a flat spot in the leader's jumping or stamina can open the door sharply for the horse nearest on his quarters; this outcome relies on Buxted Reel making a critical error or the going riding slower than the Good description implies.

watchPoints.text: Buxted Reel's ability to control the fractions entirely unchallenged is the single biggest race-shaping factor — watch whether any runner breaks unusually fast from the gate to test him early, as even brief pressure could fundamentally alter the complexion.

Most Wanted, Ask Peter and Estate Planning are all natural hold-up horses likely to be compressed into a midfield position they don't want in a field of seven — watch whether any of them get squeezed for room on Newton Abbot's tight bends and lose momentum at a crucial stage.

Run Away Joe has not run for 224 days and his recent form string includes a pulled-up and a fall — watch his jumping closely in the early stages, as a horse returning from a long absence over hurdles is a risk both for his own chance and for horses around him.

Pivotal Days is the youngest horse in the race at four years old and wore a tongue-strap last time; watch how he travels in the early stages, as any sign of greenness or reluctance to settle could see him weakening before the final flight rather than producing a finish.

races.name: Md Elite Cleaning Handicap Steeple Chase (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Breaking Cover
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator (OR 129, top weight 168lbs) trained by Anthony Honeyball, with solid Good-ground form including a recent win over 16f; 39 days since last run is fine, and the strong pace set by the front trio suits this style perfectly — arrives late and hits hard if the tempo has done its work.

runners_data.name: Centara
runners_data.note: Paul Nicholls runner (OR 127) who will press for the lead from the off; recent form shows a win but also some inconsistency (1P-645), and three rivals contesting the same early position means Centara is unlikely to get the uncontested lead that would maximise its chance — survival into the final stages depends on being the strongest of the pace trio.

runners_data.name: Obsessedwithyou
runners_data.note: Remarkably consistent (21-212 recent, 15/15 similar-going record) prominent racer trained by Jamie Snowden and ridden by Gavin Sheehan; OR 125 at 164lbs represents a manageable weight, and the ability to sit just off a hot pace rather than in it gives this horse a tactical edge that makes it the most reliably positioned runner in the field.

runners_data.name: Gore Point
runners_data.note: Six-year-old on a stunning run of form (-21111) with six wins and 11 places from 12 similar-going starts — this horse is in outstanding condition; only 5 days since last run raises a minor query, but Anthony Honeyball's 1/4 T14 record and Sam Twiston-Davies in the saddle point to confident deployment, and the hold-up style is perfectly calibrated for this pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Ice In The Veins
runners_data.note: Front-runner (OR 113, 152lbs) who will be prominent from the start but is the lowest-rated of the pace trio; 58 days since last run is the longest absence in the field, and Sarah-Jayne Davies's trainer has a T14 record of 0/5 — likely to contribute to the early pace rather than dictate it, and weakening late is the most probable outcome if the gallop is as fierce as expected.

runners_data.name: Gower Prince
runners_data.note: Jonjo & A.J. O'Neill runner (OR 108, 147lbs) who has been racing frequently (12 days since last run) and goes in headgear; recent form of 6P2-21 shows ability but also a tendency to underperform, and as the lowest-OR pace-presser in the field, Gower Prince is the most likely of the front three to crack under sustained pressure from the better-weighted rivals.

races.paceDynamic: Three confirmed front-runners — Centara, Ice In The Veins, and Gower Prince — will contest the lead from the outset over 2m½f at Newton Abbot on Good ground, making a strong, genuine gallop virtually certain. Centara (Paul Nicholls, OR 127) is likely to be the most aggressive of the trio, with Ice In The Veins and Gower Prince pressing hard enough to ensure no single horse dictates on their own terms, creating a punishing, attritional tempo across the fences. The hold-up horses Breaking Cover and Gore Point, plus the prominent Obsessedwithyou, will be able to stalk a hot pace and arrive with their stamina reserves intact. This race shape firmly favours patient, well-handled hold-up and prominent runners who can travel smoothly behind the heat and produce a sustained finish — Obsessedwithyou, Gore Point, and Breaking Cover are all built for exactly this scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way pace battle burns out the front-runners from the third fence, leaving stamina and a late surge to decide it.
scenarios.body: Centara, Ice In The Veins, and Gower Prince fight for supremacy throughout, setting a true gallop that depletes their reserves before the final fence; Gore Point and Breaking Cover, tracking the pace economically, are poised to sweep through in the closing stages. Gore Point's remarkable recent five-timer run and Breaking Cover's proven hold-up aptitude over similar trips make both ideal beneficiaries of this collapsed front-running scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Thrives
scenarios.trigger: If Obsessedwithyou secures a clean prominent position and the pace is strong but not catastrophically fast, allowing a measured traveller to win a stamina contest.
scenarios.body: Obsessedwithyou (OR 125, 5 wins and 12 places from 15 similar-going runs) slots in behind the leaders without becoming embroiled in the pace battle, travels with controlled energy, and produces a powerful staying effort from two out. Gavin Sheehan's tactical judgment suits this patient-prominent role and the horse's consistent 2/1/2 form sequence underlines its reliability under pressure.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace trio — most plausibly Centara — is able to assert early dominance and the others fade, leaving a single leader to control the contest.
scenarios.body: Centara has the highest OR (127) of the three front-runners and the Paul Nicholls handler connection brings class at this level; if Ice In The Veins and Gower Prince are the ones to crack under the pressure they help create, Centara could slip clear from the last and hold on. This shape requires the other pace rivals to tire before Centara does — possible but against the weight of evidence given the competitive OR gap and three-horse dynamic.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Errors Disrupt
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or fallers among the front-running trio reshuffle the race dramatically and a beneficiary steals an uncontested lead.
scenarios.body: With three horses fighting for position over fences at pace, the probability of a costly mistake, unseating, or pile-up at an early fence is elevated compared to a cleaner race shape; any horse who avoids the chaos and finds daylight early benefits. Gore Point's freshness (only 5 days since last run) and class edge makes it the likeliest opportunist if the front three falter through misadventure rather than attrition.

watchPoints.text: Three-way pace battle between Centara, Ice In The Veins, and Gower Prince over fences on Good ground dramatically raises the risk of a jumping error or interference at an early fence — monitor closely from flag-fall.
Gore Point has run just 5 days ago — watch for any sign of residual fatigue or below-par jumping in the second half of the race, as a quick turnaround at this level can catch horses out late.

Obsessedwithyou must secure a clean prominent position early without becoming part of the front-running melee — if Gavin Sheehan is pushed wider or back by the pace trio jostling, the horse's tactical advantage is significantly reduced.

Breaking Cover (168lbs top weight, 39 days off) must be given a patient ride by Chad Bament (5lb claimer) — any impatience from an inexperienced conditional in a strongly-run race could see the horse expend energy too early and fail to deliver the late thrust this style depends on.

Ice In The Veins is 58 days off and the trainer has a T14 strike rate of 0/5 — note any early signs of ring-rustiness or laboured jumping, which would confirm a likely weakener from three out rather than a pace-setting force to the finish.

races.name: Compwiz Ltd - It Solutions For Business Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Final Entry
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer with a win and two places from 12 similar-going runs, the 5lb claim from Rian Corcoran is a significant asset over a marathon trip; 42 days between runs is not a concern for David Pipe, and the horse's best recent form — a win at 26f on Good — matches today's conditions well.

runners_data.name: Jack The Savage
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner with an outstanding 13/15 similar-going record and two wins at this sort of trip; Laura Horsfall's yard has had no runners in the last 14 days so draw no trainer pattern, but Sean Bowen's booking is a clear upgrade — 53 days off and the tp headgear retained.

runners_data.name: My Girl Katie
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins and four wins from 11 similar-going starts make her a serious player; Grace Harris's stable is firing (3/15 over 14 days) and only 5 days since her last run needs monitoring for freshness, though her recent form string of 1-1 suggests she thrives with quick turnarounds at 26f Good.

runners_data.name: Touchwoodexpress
runners_data.note: A prominent runner who has won at 26f on Good ground but recent form figures of 6-7-6-5 before a latest win suggest inconsistency; the v headgear is retained and Sam Twiston-Davies riding for his family yard is always significant, though 57 days between runs and a winless trainer strike-rate over 14 days temper enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Alberts Bay
runners_data.note: James Best takes the ride on a horse 92 days absent and whose last four runs show he has not raced beyond 22f, making this 26f trip a genuine query; three of his last four runs on Good produced a place, but a fall in recent form and the extended layoff make him one to watch rather than rely upon.

runners_data.name: Man Oh Man
runners_data.note: Genuinely a hold-up type by nature, he has been pushed into a midfield slot on the map because the field's rear is overcrowded — at a trip well beyond his most competitive 18f-20f range, his chance is doubly compressed; Bryan Carver rides and the form string of 5-9-2-7-8 over shorter trips does not inspire for 3m2½f.

runners_data.name: Blue Siam
runners_data.note: A 4-year-old tackling a 26f hurdle for the first time, Blue Siam's natural instinct is to come from behind but the pace map has him shown in midfield because genuine closers already fill the back — the combination of inexperience at the trip, a style-fit penalty, and Ellis Collier's 5lb claim make this a speculative each-way profile at best.

races.paceDynamic: Jack The Savage is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 3m2½f contest and, with no genuine rival willing to press him from the front, he should establish a comfortable, metronomic gallop on Good ground that suits his record of 13 place finishes from 15 similar-going starts. My Girl Katie and Touchwoodexpress are both prominent types who will track him through the early stages, creating a small lead group that sets a fair but not frantic tempo over this marathon trip. The real complexity here is that Blue Siam and Man Oh Man are natural hold-up horses who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field's back-end is already crowded — neither is likely to get as far back as they prefer, meaning they will race slightly out of their comfort zone and their finishing efforts may be compromised as a result. This race shape — an uncontested front-runner setting a sustainable pace — strongly favours prominent racers who can track economically and pounce late, or hold-up horses with genuine stamina and a clean passage, not those forced to race outside their natural rhythm.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jack The Savage Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Jack The Savage bowls along uncontested and the pace is fair enough to expose the stamina limits of prominent rivals.
scenarios.body: Jack The Savage dictates from the front on a going surface he handles well (13/15 similar-going), and if the race unfolds at a controlled tempo he can ration his effort over the marathon trip and punch clear at the last; his 2W5P record on similar ground speaks to this profile. Prominent types My Girl Katie and Touchwoodexpress are best placed to chase him home if they track efficiently, with the 4W6P similar-going record of My Girl Katie making her the most dangerous pursuer.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Wear Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens through the middle section and Jack The Savage's lead erodes before the final flight.
scenarios.body: My Girl Katie — fresh off back-to-back wins and with a 4W6P similar-going record — or Touchwoodexpress could reel in a tiring Jack The Savage if the gallop proves more demanding than it looks, with both horses positioned to strike from a stalking role. This scenario suits runners who travel strongly in the lead group and have the stamina for a tough finish at 3m2½f on Good turf.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace truly collapses in the final mile and a late surge becomes viable for those forced to race wide of their preferred position.
scenarios.body: Final Entry is the most credible hold-up beneficiary here, with a genuine win over similar 26f Good-ground trips and Rian Corcoran claiming 5lb, giving him a potential late edge if the field strings out and a gap appears; Alberts Bay is 92 days fresh and may find form arriving late. Blue Siam and Man Oh Man are natural closers but both are racing out of role at this longer trip and with style-fit penalties, reducing their claims materially in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Carnage — Attrition Finishes
scenarios.trigger: If the 3m2½f trip combined with Good ground causes multiple errors or fallers and the race becomes a test of pure jumping and survival.
scenarios.body: Over this extreme distance any jumping error at a critical hurdle can prove decisive, and horses with proven jumping reliability such as My Girl Katie (consistent form figures of 1-1-1-2-3) or Final Entry would benefit from rivals departing. Jack The Savage's age (9) and previous fall history introduce a small but real risk that the race is turned on its head entirely.

watchPoints.text: Jack The Savage sets the pace entirely unchallenged — if Sean Bowen elects to steal a significant lead early, prominent rivals My Girl Katie and Touchwoodexpress must decide whether to close or gift him daylight that may never be recovered over 3m2½f.

My Girl Katie runs just 5 days after her last outing; monitor paddock behaviour and early racing demeanour — horses returning this quickly can over-race or fail to settle, which at this marathon trip would be fatal to her stamina.

Blue Siam and Man Oh Man are both racing out of their natural hold-up role and at trips beyond their form base — if either is seen pulling hard in an unfamiliar midfield position from the start, discount their finishing effort accordingly.

Alberts Bay's 92-day absence and step up to a career-longest trip means his jumping sharpness should be watched at the early hurdles; a blunder at any stage could end his race prematurely and disrupt the rhythm of horses tracking close behind.

Final Entry's headgear note (tv — tongue tie and visor) combined with Rian Corcoran's 5lb claim means the horse carries least weight in the field effectively — watch where he is positioned at halfway, as a clear run from midfield late could make the claim decisive.

races.name: Marilyn And Millie's Retirement Handicap Steeple Chase (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Quick Sharpener
runners_data.note: Held up at OR=111 with Gavin Sheehan aboard, he has good recent form on Good and has placed at 23f — the step up to 2m5f looks fine, and sitting just off Mcgregors Charge in second or third will be his natural position; 57 days off is worth noting but Snowden's yard is in decent nick (T14: 2/4), and tongue-strap is retained from last run.

runners_data.name: Lady Kara
runners_data.note: Exceptionally consistent on Good going (11/12 similar-going record) and comes here on a hot streak of three wins from four starts, though an unseated rider mars the recent form string; Charlie Hammond will likely slot her into a prominent pitch just off the leader, and at just five years old she holds strong upside, but the hood (h) is new headgear and could be a variable to watch.

runners_data.name: Thickthorn Tom
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton partners a horse in excellent form — five runs all producing a win or place — and Dan Skelton's yard has fired in 7 winners from 26 over 14 days; held up by profile, he needs the pace to be honest enough to bring him into the race, and Good ground is clearly his forte, but 2m5f is the longest trip he's tackled and stamina must be proven.

runners_data.name: It's A Breeze
runners_data.note: Paul Nicholls runner who has won twice at 21f on Good and steps up in trip here; held up by style with a 5lb-claiming amateur in Paddy Hanlon, and the Nicholls yard has had no runners in the last 14 days — a cold-yard angle worth flagging; the horse has fallen (F) recently too, so jumping confidence and jockey inexperience at this level are mild concerns.

runners_data.name: Mcgregors Charge
runners_data.note: Clear front-runner who will likely set the entire shape of this contest from the first fence; OR=81 gives a significant weight advantage over the field and 12 days since his last run is a fresh return, though trainer Gundry is quiet (T14: 0/1); his recent form shows a 2nd last time out and he's proven on Good turf, but his ability to sustain the gallop over 2m5f against higher-rated rivals is the key question.

races.paceDynamic: Mcgregors Charge is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and will stride into the lead from the outset, setting a solo, uncontested gallop over 2m5f of good ground at Newton Abbot. With no other horse in the field carrying front-running tendencies, the pace is entirely in Mcgregors Charge's hands — likely honest but not brutal, meaning rivals in behind will travel comfortably without being stretched. Quick Sharpener and Lady Kara will track from prominent positions just off the leader, while Thickthorn Tom and It's A Breeze will be held up in the rear, dependent on a strong enough gallop to close into. The race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just behind Mcgregors Charge, stay close enough to pounce over the final fences, and avoid the risk of getting too much to do from the back — a sustainable lead will not force the hold-up horses into a winning position unless they are travelling with exceptional ease.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Mcgregors Charge sets a steady-to-fair gallop and Quick Sharpener or Lady Kara track efficiently before asserting from the last two fences.
scenarios.body: Mcgregors Charge controls the tempo without being pressured, allowing the prominent horses to coast in behind and save ground, then pick him off as his stamina wanes on the run-in over the final 2f; the Good ground suits both prominent types who carry strong recent form at this going, and the distance is squarely within their profiles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to string the field out and the hold-up horses travel powerfully enough to close the gap over the final mile.
scenarios.body: Thickthorn Tom in particular has been in fine form with a string of placed and winning efforts at similar distances on Good ground, and Harry Skelton's positional awareness could allow him to make significant headway from the final turn if the front has gone too fast; It's A Breeze has winning form over this trip on Good and could also benefit, though the pair face a real risk of being left with too much to do if pace is modest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Defies Them All
scenarios.trigger: If Mcgregors Charge dictates a perfectly judged solo tempo, builds an insurmountable lead, and jumps well enough to hold the prominent challengers at bay to the line.
scenarios.body: Running from just OR=81, Mcgregors Charge carries a significant weight advantage and the 12-day turnaround suggests trainer Polly Gundry believes the horse is in top form; if the prominent pair misjudge their challenge or make jumping errors, the leader could steal enough of a break to hold on, with Good ground and turf-headgear form supporting the scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Errors Shuffle The Pack
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors among the front-runners or prominent horses cause interference or losses of momentum that hand an unexpected advantage to horses further back.
scenarios.body: Newton Abbot's fences can punish over-confident or rusty jumpers, and with Lady Kara having a U (unseated) in recent form and Quick Sharpener's consistency rated as mixed, a fence-related incident could scramble the order; Thickthorn Tom and It's A Breeze, held up and less exposed to early scrimmaging, could benefit from a chaotic mid-race passage.

watchPoints.text: Lady Kara's new hood (headgear debut) is unproven — monitor her behaviour in the early stages, as a keen or unsettled response could blow her chance in a race where conserving energy is paramount over 2m5f.

Mcgregors Charge's front-running role is uncontested but he is rated 26-30lbs below the top three rivals — if prominent horses Quick Sharpener or Lady Kara press him from the third fence, his lead could evaporate rapidly in the final mile.

It's A Breeze has a fall in recent form and is ridden by a 5lb claimer in Paddy Hanlon — watch the horse at the early fences for any jumping hesitancy, which could cost vital ground given the hold-up style requires late momentum.

Thickthorn Tom's stamina over 2m5f is unproven — his best form is clustered at 19f-21f, and though he is clearly fit and in form, watch whether he is still travelling easily from the fourth-last fence or beginning to flatten out.

The T14 form for Dr Richard Newland & Jamie Insole (0/8) is cold — Lady Kara's strong recent form is the overriding positive, but the trainer angle is a quiet note that betting markets may not have fully priced in.

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Donnie Azoff
runners_data.note: Jamie Snowden's 10-year-old has a strong affinity with good ground (13 from 15 in similar going) and won over an identical trip last time out 46 days ago, giving the yard sufficient recovery time; a natural hold-up horse, Isabelle Ryder (5lb claim) retains the ride, and the horse's consistency at 2m2f+ on turf makes this a legitimate opportunity if the pace is strong enough to reel in.

runners_data.name: Beorma
runners_data.note: Dan and Harry Skelton's seven-year-old carries the race on its shoulders as the lone pace-setter, boasting a sparkling recent sequence of five wins including four consecutive, yet the two-day turnaround since last run is an unusual quick-fire move that demands scrutiny; the STYLE_FIT flag suggests it may be racing out of its most comfortable role here, and any stamina drain from front-running duties over 18+ furlongs could be costly late.

runners_data.name: King Of The Bronx
runners_data.note: A five-year-old returning from 373 days off the track, which is the primary concern here — that layoff dwarfs anything else in the field and introduces massive fitness unknowns for Syd Hosie's yard; the ⚠ fade flag compounds the worry, as this horse has historically been vulnerable in the closing stages even when fit, and the one win on good ground came over a shorter 16f trip.

runners_data.name: Ellerton
runners_data.note: Joe Tizzard's six-year-old has good ground form (2W, 5P on similar going) and placed over course-relevant distances, including a second over 22f last time; though shown in midfield on the pace map for display purposes, this is a genuine hold-up horse whose natural style is to come from the rear — the STYLE_FIT tag means it may struggle if this race doesn't set up with enough tempo to make a sustained late run viable.

races.paceDynamic: Beorma, trained by Dan Skelton and ridden by Harry Skelton, is the lone confirmed front-runner in a field of just four and will set a solo, controlled gallop from the outset over 2m2½f on good ground at Newton Abbot. With no genuine rival to press them early, the Skeltons' horse can dictate a sustainable, unhurried tempo that keeps the race within its comfort zone — a scenario that historically favours the pace-setter who can also jump well and quicken from the front. The remaining three runners — Donnie Azoff, King Of The Bronx, and Ellerton — are all hold-up types by profile, meaning the entire chasing pack will be ridden conservatively off the pace, likely bunched together through the middle stages waiting for the final climb. This race shape heavily favours a patient, well-timed hold-up finisher who can sustain a run from two out and pick up on the testing final bend, provided Beorma does not steal the race on the bridle by setting an undetectably strong early pace; the field holds more hold-up types than genuine prominent racers can contest, and Beorma is the only horse likely to secure a front position — Ellerton, despite being mapped to midfield for display purposes, is a true hold-up horse and will not challenge for early real estate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Beorma Front, Closers Late
scenarios.trigger: If Beorma leads comfortably and hold-up horses pick their moment two out on the run to the last.
scenarios.body: Beorma sets a controlled solo gallop, giving the hold-up brigade a target to aim at from mid-race; the closers begin their runs rounding the final bend, and the winner is determined by who sustains their effort up the home straight most effectively.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Beorma Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Beorma, uncontested, gradually increases tempo from halfway and reaches the last with too big a lead to peg back.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing or able to track Beorma aggressively, Harry Skelton can dictate every change in pace without answer, stealing margins imperceptibly through the final mile; the hold-up horses, having conserved energy for a challenge that arrives too late, cannot close the gap up the run-in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up War On Flat
scenarios.trigger: If Beorma weakens abruptly after the second-last and the three hold-up horses sprint for the line simultaneously.
scenarios.body: A collapse in Beorma's stamina — perhaps linked to the quick turnaround of just two days since last run — throws the race open to an all-in sprint home between the hold-up horses; the one with the best finishing gears and freshest legs on this good ground wins a tactical scramble.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rough Jumping Plays Havoc
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors shuffle the order dramatically and the race degenerates into an attrition-based test.
scenarios.body: With King Of The Bronx carrying significant jumping fragility and Beorma risking errors from front-running fatigue, a race punctuated by mistakes creates a chaotic finish where stamina and error-free jumping rather than tactical nous decides the outcome.

watchPoints.text: Beorma's two-day turnaround is the single biggest risk factor in the race — watch whether Harry Skelton has any control issues in the early stages or whether the horse jumps flat through the back, which would signal stamina trouble before the home turn.

King Of The Bronx returns from 373 days absent and has a documented tendency to fade late — watch its jumping and body language from three out, as any sign of distress early will render it a non-factor long before the finish.

With three hold-up horses waiting on a single front-runner, watch whether any of the jockeys — particularly Isabelle Ryder on Donnie Azoff — blink and creeps closer to Beorma earlier than planned, potentially turning the race into a two-horse duel that burns out the closers.

Ellerton's true hold-up profile means Brendan Powell will need a genuinely strong pace to deliver a meaningful late run — if Beorma dawdles, watch Ellerton's position two out to gauge whether the horse is travelling within itself or already under pressure without cover.
